content.title: About
content.content: Prepared yellow mustard (item 5584) is a classic tangy condiment made from ground yellow mustard seeds, vinegar, salt and spices. It has a bright yellow colour, distinctive aroma and moderate heat, suitable for dressing salads, sandwiches, marinades and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yellow mustard is traditionally made from Sinapis alba seeds, which are milder than black mustard seeds.
The first commercial mustard in Russia is considered "Petrov's Mustard", introduced in the early 19th century.
Mustard seeds are rich in glucosinolates that convert to pungent mustard oil when crushed.
In the United States, yellow mustard is the standard topping for hot‑dogs and hamburgers.
A small amount of sugar is often added to yellow mustard to balance its sharpness.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Mustard seeds contain selenium and vitamin E, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Mustard enzymes stimulate bile production, aiding the digestion of fats.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Mustard provides magnesium, calcium and iron, essential for muscle and bone health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One tablespoon of prepared mustard contains about 15 kcal, making it a light alternative to richer sauces.

items.title: Provides probiotic compounds
items.content: Fermentation of mustard seeds can promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Mustard allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mustard seeds, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared mustard often contains added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should use it in moderation.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: The sharpness of mustard can aggravate gastritis or heartburn in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Large amounts of mustard may affect the action of anticoagulants due to its vitamin K content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use mustard as a salad dressing, meat marinade, sauce ingredient, sandwich spread, or flavor boost for cooked dishes. It can be mixed with honey for a sweet‑spicy glaze or added to a chicken brine to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store mustard in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator. Properly kept, it retains its flavor and aroma for up to 12 months. Discard if the colour changes, an off‑smell develops, or mold appears.
